Pakistan wants to become the world's sixth-largest economy before 2050. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has brought forward by more than 25 years Goldman Sachs' projection that Pakistan could reach the milestone by 2075. But can the country really pull off this economic transformation?
But Pakistan faces a formidable economic reality: a heavy debt burden, dependence on the International Monetary Fund (IMF), political instability and security challenges.
